The test image shows a close-up of a soybean stem at a node with **gray/white fluffy material** at the node junction, surrounded by yellowing leaves. Key features: green hairy stem, gray fungal-looking growth at the node, late-season senescent leaves.

Top candidates: Diaporthe (pycnidia at nodes), Brown_Stem_Rot (brown pith at nodes), Tobacco_Streak_Virus (dead streaks at nodes). Let me check references.

**Key observations from test image:**
- Close-up of soybean stem at a node
- **Gray/white fluffy material specifically at the node junction** — localized abnormal growth
- Otherwise green, hairy stem (normal)
- Surrounding leaves are yellowing/senescent (late-season)

**Analysis:**
- **Diaporthe**: Would show black flask-shaped pycnidia in rows — doesn't match gray fluffy material
- **Brown Stem Rot**: Would show brown pith internally — the gray at the node surface doesn't match well
- **Tobacco Streak Virus**: Description includes "bud and leaf proliferation," "discoloration and dead streaks at nodes" — TSV reference (bottom-left panel) clearly shows abnormal proliferating tissue at node junctions similar to what's visible

The gray fluffy material at the node junction in the test image closely matches the TSV reference showing nodal tissue proliferation/discoloration, combined with the yellowing leaves in a late-season context.
